before: A minimal reproduction is the smallest example you can find that still demonstrates the same failure. It makes the cause easier to isolate and the result easier for another person to verify.

A page with twenty components fails when an empty list is passed to total(). Remove unrelated rendering while keeping the empty-list call. If the failure disappears, restore the last removed dependency and continue carefully.

reduce without an initial value cannot choose a starting accumulator from an empty array. The function call is the trigger, [] is the boundary input, and the thrown error is the observed failure. Adding an initial 0 is a possible fix, but first preserve the failing example as a regression check.
Changed situation: Removing a component makes the failure disappear. Is the smaller example ready to report as a reproduction?
A useful reproduction preserves the observed failure. Size reduction is secondary to fidelity.
after: A minimal reproduction is a small example that still shows a bug. It helps another person repeat the problem and inspect its cause.
Remove unrelated code a little at a time. After each removal, rerun the input that caused the failure.
reduce combines entries into a running result. Without a starting value, it takes the first entry as the start. An empty array has no first entry, so this call throws an error.
If the wanted total for an empty list is 0, supplying an initial 0 to reduce can fix this case. First keep a test for the failing input so the same bug is caught later.
If removing a part makes the failure disappear, the smaller example no longer reproduces the bug. Restore what is needed before sharing it as a reproduction.
